To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coexpression of cytokine and a suicide gene by EBV-CTL enhances their expansion in vitro and in a SCID mouse model and their antitumor effect in a mouse xenograft model.
transgenic expression by CTLs of lymphokines that are known to stimulate the growth of T cells, and the inclusion of a safety switch, may enhance the efficacy and safety of adoptive T-cell therapy.
the co-expression of lymphokines and a suicide gene in tumor-specific CTLs increases the antitumor effect and safety of this approach for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of cytokine and/or suicide genes to improve the efficacy of CTL therapy.
the development of a new generation of adoptive immunotherapy for cancer based on transgenic expression of cytokine genes by tumor-specific CTLs.
the development of a novel gene-modified CTLs for the treatment of EBV-associated tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coexpression of cytokine and inducible suicide genes in EBV-specific T cells may enhance the activity and the safety of these cells for the treatment of patients with EBV-associated malignancies.
the co-expression of cytokine genes and a suicide gene in EBV-CTL is an effective and safe strategy to enhance their activity in the treatment of EBV-related malignancies.
co-expression of cytokine genes with suicide genes in tumor-specific T cells is a safe and promising strategy that could be used to increase the therapeutic potential of adoptive T-cell therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of cytokine and inducible caspace-9 genes can be a promising approach for the development of adoptively transferred CTLs with enhanced antitumor effect and safety.
the combination of cytokine genes with suicide genes in tumor-specific T cells may provide an efficient and safe approach to cancer immunotherapy.
the co-expression of cytokine genes with a suicide gene can be used to improve the activity of tumor-specific T cells while reducing the risk of autoimmunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transgenic expression and inducible expression of cytokine genes can enhance the efficacy of CTLs and that this strategy may be used to improve the efficacy of CTL-based immunotherapies.

transgenic expression by CTLs of lymphokines, such as IL-2, IL-15, or IL-21, that enhance the expansion and antitumor activity of these cells may overcome limitations in the clinical use of adoptively transferred T cells.
the coexpression of a lymphokine and a suicide gene in T cells may enhance the activity and improve the safety of adoptive immunotherapy.
